raw_response:
Ai, let me think through this year's plan. It's just me now — my son works in Handan, my wife passed a few years back. 62 years old, 40 years on this same ground. The body doesn't bend like it used to, but the land still has to be worked.

I've got my 15 mu split the way I've done for a while now. Most of it — about 10 mu — is in stevia. The company (the one out of Feixiang) brings the seedlings and buys back the dried leaf; they take the seedling money off the top when they pay, so I don't have to put cash up front. That arrangement is why an old man alone can still farm 15 mu. The other 5 mu I keep in wheat and maize like everyone else around here, so I have my own grain and a little to sell.

**Stevia (10 mu).** I've been doing stevia maybe 8 years now. Transplant in late April after the soil warms. The company tells us what fertilizer to use but I just do what's always worked — two bags of 15-15-15 for the 10 mu before planting, then one bag of urea after the first cut to push the regrowth. I cut twice, once in late July and once around late September. The cutting is hard — I hire three or four neighbors for a couple of days each time and pay them 100 yuan a day. The well goes on three times if the summer's dry, more if it's a bad year. My neighbor Old Liu does more water but his electric bill eats him up.

**Wheat (5 mu).** Plant mid-October after I clear the maize. I know this crop in my bones. Put down the compound when I sow — about one and a half bags for the five mu — and if the wheat looks yellow around jointing in March, I topdress some urea. Last spring it was yellow, I added urea, it came back nicely. I'll do the same if I see it again. Water before winter so the roots go deep, water again after jointing, and once more at filling if it hasn't rained. Hire the combine when harvest comes — 50 yuan a mu, not bad.

**Maize (5 mu).** Straight into the wheat stubble in mid-June, no tilling. No time, no strength. Hire the fellow with the planter for 30 yuan a mu; he does it in an afternoon. Compound at planting, urea when it's knee-high if the rain's been decent. If July goes dry I'll pump once, no more than that — water costs money and maize is pretty tough.

For pesticide I just use the herbicide everyone uses. Bugs I deal with if I see them but I don't spray just in case. I don't have extra money to waste on what might not happen.

That's the plan. Same as most years. When you're 62 and alone, you don't try new things without a good reason.
